newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-SPENCER MIGHT REPLACE MEHRTENS FOR GOOD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPENCER MIGHT REPLACE MEHRTENS FOR GOOD.

text.p: All Black coach John Hart hinted on Wednesday that Andrew Mehrtens may lose his position as New Zealand's number one fly-half to arch rival Carlos Spencer.
Mehrtens, struggling to recuperate from a hamstring strain, has been ruled out of the crunch test against old foe Australia at Christchurch on Saturday.
Spencer will again take Mehrtens's pivotal position in the All Black midfield, as he has done so effectively in the last two tests against Argentina.
Hart said Mehrtens may yet warm the bench on Saturday, but Spencer had made great strides at test level and was ready to take on the Wallabies.
"I think Carlos Spencer has developed considerably and the value of him having had those two tests is immeasurable to us," Hart said.
"He (Mehrtens) was the incumbent but we have no hesitation about playing Carlos Spencer."
Asked if Mehrtens was still considered the best fly-half in the country, Hart said the gap between Mehrtens and Spencer had narrowed.
"I think they're a lot closer than they were," he said.
It remained to be seen whether Mehrtens would reclaim his position in the starting 15 after his return to full fitness.
"That's a decision for after the weekend," Hart said.
While not as reliable a goalkicker as Mehrtens, nor as visionary, Spencer has stamped his flair on the All Blacks this season, scoring 53 points in just two tests.

He has been labelled flashy and arrogant for his overt confidence, but Spencer's handling skills and ability to find gaps where none seem to exist have also seen the 21-year-old widely acknowledged as an exceptionally talented player.
Spencer dazzled British rugby fans last year when he scored a brilliant individual try in the New Zealand Barbarians' 34-19 win over England.
But Australia will be the acid test for the young Spencer, who still must prove himself at top level before Hart relegates Mehrtens indefinitely to the reserves.
